hypothesis.hypothesis:
IPC-neutral Fmax change, three cuts, built and timed in this order on all
three placement options against a same-session baseline.

A. EX-result capture bypass (delete the EX head forward muxes).
   When ID/EX captures consumer C (!hold, !kill) the producer P in EX leaves
   EX at the same edge (hold_id = dmem_stall | ex_busy covers both ways P can
   stay), so P's rd value is exactly the combinational `alu_result` of that
   cycle (ALU / link / muldiv result at md_done). A LOAD in EX is a load-use
   kill, so it never needs this leg. Therefore drive the ID/EX operand D
   inputs with a third source instead of registering fwd_*_ex selects:
      rs1_val.D = m_rs1_ex              ? alu_result : rs1_byp
      rs2_val.D = m_rs2_ex              ? alu_result : rs2_byp
      op_a.D    = (m_rs1_ex & a_is_reg) ? alu_result : op_a_old
      op_b.D    = (m_rs2_ex & b_is_reg) ? alu_result : op_b_old
   (m_*_ex already contains ex_reg_write_next = reg_write & !jalr_bad &
   !flush_q, so a squashed / trapping producer is never forwarded.) EX then
   reads in.rs1_val / in.rs2_val / in.op_a / in.op_b straight from flops:
   fwd_rs1_ex / fwd_rs2_ex / fwd_a_ex / fwd_b_ex and the four 32-bit 2:1 muxes
   disappear from the head of the adder carry, barrel shifter, branch compare
   (-> flush_q, the option-0 worst path), rs1+imm address adder and muldiv
   operand latch. The mux reappears at the tail, but there it merges with the
   ALU's final OR: D = s_ex ? (x | y) : (sel_ld ? load_data : early) is one
   Gowin CLS (two LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5, no routed net in between), so the ALU loop
   ID/EX.op -> adder/shifter -> AND-OR -> ID/EX.op loses one LUT plus one
   routed net, and the load-data / early legs keep their single final level
   (they only gain the in-slice MUX2). Operands are now stable in ID/EX for
   as long as the consumer sits in EX (dmem stall, M-op busy), which is
   strictly simpler than today's "select stays exact while held" argument.
   EX/MEM.alu_result still captures alu_result for the MEM->ID leg and rd_val.

   A2 (only if `ID/EX.alu_sub -> carry -> alu_result` is still the worst
   path after A, since that path never went through the head mux): apply
   r4s1's rule "a flop-selected mux belongs AFTER arithmetic" to add/sub.
   Build a + b and a - b as two parallel carry chains straight from the
   operand flops and select them with registered one-hot sel_add / sel_sub
   legs of the existing AND-OR (SLT/SLTU take bit 32 of the subtract chain),
   so the fanout-33 alu_sub net leaves the carry chain (+33 ALU cells).

B. Regfile written at the MEM/WB capture edge (delete the write-first bypass).
   Write regs[EX/MEM.rd] with the MEM/WB.rd_val D value (mem_to_reg ?
   load_data : alu_result) and we = trap-gated reg_write & valid & !dmem_stall
   & rd != 0, i.e. one cycle earlier than today. The instruction in WB has
   then already been written when ID reads, so the `w_do && w_addr == rs_addr
   ? w_data : ...` leg (two 5-bit comparators + 64 mux LUTs, one LUT level

title: Six-stage split: registered IF/ID instruction register, with r7s2's successor-word table kept entirely on the fetch side (iStall hidden, decode still starts at a flop)
motivation:
The only pool left that is larger than the +4.6% bar is the imem bus:
~22% not-ready, ~0.8M of the champion's 4,283,613 CoreMark cycles.
r7s2 proved it can be hidden: a PC-indexed successor-word table (NIT,
256 x {tag, dir, word} LUT-RAM, read by pc_q a cycle ahead) ran CoreMark
in 3,536,081 cycles (+21% iter/cycle), formal + cosim green. It lost on
Fmax (117.5 -> 105.0 MHz) for two structural reasons, both of which get
worse on today's 130.2 MHz core:
  1. the head mux `cur_instr = use_nb ? nb_instr_q : imem_data` sits in
     front of the whole merged IF+ID cycle. r7s0 left `imem_data ->
     regfile read -> op_a/op_b D` co-critical at 7.68 ns, so one more LUT
     + a fanout-32 select net there is ~0.7 ns (<= ~119 MHz) on arrival;
  2. `pc_q -> NIT RAM read -> 22-bit tag compare -> nb_v_q` (31 cells) was
     the worst path on option 0 (88 MHz).
Neither is a depth problem that a mux reshuffle fixes; the word select
simply does not belong in the same cycle as decode. Arithmetic on logged
numbers (not a measurement): 3.54M cycles + one extra bubble on each of
the ~137k remaining redirects = ~3.68M cycles, which is 354 at 130.2 MHz,
340 at 125, 326 at 120; the 318.0 bar is cleared down to ~117 MHz
(-10% Fmax), a far wider margin than any fetch-buffer build had (~6%).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the merged IF+ID cycle with a real IF/ID register and put ALL
stall-hiding logic in front of it. Decode, regfile read, load-use and
the op_a/op_b pre-mux then start at `ir_q` flops exactly as they start
at the bench's imem_data flops today (no head mux, no new sink), and
the F -> ID/EX families (`fa -> adders -> btarget`, `PHT -> pred_taken
-> redir_c1/c0`) end at IF/ID flops instead.

F stage (if_stage.sv; pc_q / fa / fa_inc / PHT / tgt adders unchanged):
  word select by a FLOP, validity separate (control only):
    cur_instr  = imem_ready ? imem_data : nb_instr_q   // syn_keep
    have_instr = imem_ready | use_nb
  cur_instr feeds the raw pre-decode, imm_j/imm_b and the IF/ID D input.
  The 2:1 only brings the immediates level with the existing `fa` mux
  (r7s2 measured no steering path in its top 5). A garbage cur_instr
  (!have_instr) is never consumed: pc_q holds and IF/ID takes valid=0.
  NIT = r7s2's table (AW=8, LUT-RAM {tag, dir, word}, 2^AW reset valid
  flops, index pc_q[AW-1:0], fill from prev_fa_q / prev_tk_q / adv_q
  flops when adv_q && !flush_q && imem_ready && !use_nb), but the hit
  compare is moved OUT of the RAM-read cycle - register the raw read:
    nb_instr_q <= stall ? cur_instr : t_word
    nb_tag_q   <= t_tag;  nb_dir_q <= t_dir;  nb_tk_q <= pred_taken
    nb_val_q   <= !stall && t_valid && !flush_q
    nb_skid_q  <=  stall && have_instr            // 1-word skid, as r7s2
    use_nb = (nb_skid_q | (nb_val_q && nb_tag_q == prev_fa_q[29:AW]
                           && nb_dir_q == nb_tk_q)) && !flush_q
  so the lookup cycle is pc_q -> RAM16 + 16:1 mux -> flop (no compare, no
  late pred_taken term except its own 1 flop) and use_nb is a ~3-level
  flop-only compare that feeds ONLY have_instr -> stall_if, in parallel
  with (and no deeper than) the load-use compare. It never selects data.

IF/ID register (new, in if_stage or id_stage): {valid, instr, pc, pc4,
  tgt, pred_taken, pht, fl}; enable = !hold_id && !load_use (D advances);
  valid <= have_instr && !flush_q_squash (see below). Data fields
  clock-enable only, valid reset to 0. Keep stall_if = !have_instr |
  hold_id | load_use (no bubble collapse in the first build).
D stage = today's id_stage verbatim, `in` now the registered bundle;
  hazard_unit takes rs1/rs2 from ir_q and
    kill_id = load_use | !ifid.valid | flush_q
  (flush_q is a flop; the instruction in D in the flush cycle is
  wrong-path, the one in EX is squashed by ex_stage as today).
Redirect becomes 2 bubbles: flush cycle fetches flush_pc_q from the bus
  only (use_nb = 0), its word reaches D one cycle later. The word fetched
  in the flush cycle is correct-path, so IF/ID captures it normally; the
  flush cycle never holds (unchanged argument: EX/MEM holds the branch).
  `fl` / bp_train / redir_c1 = c0 = 1 for the unfollowed JAL carry over
  unchanged through IF/ID.
RVFI / formal: rvfi_insn is the executed word, the formal wrapper makes
  imem_data symbolic per cycle, so a table word is just another legal
  stream (r7s2: 53/53 at AW=6 in ~7 min; reg_ch0 is the long pole - run
  formal FIRST at AW=6, `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash
  formal/run_all.sh`, then `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`).

Order of work and decision rule:
  1. IF/ID register + 2-bubble redirect with NO table (imem_stall =
     !imem_ready): formal, CoreMark cycles (expect ~4.42M), one timing
     run. This isolates what the register alone does to Fmax (it removes
     two F -> ID/EX families; any gain here is banked for step 2).
  2. Add the NIT (r7s2's RTL was not merged and no branch of it exists;
     its design + implementation notes are in experiments/log.jsonl
     under hyp-20261125-003-r7s2 - rebuild from those). CoreMark cycles
     at AW=8 (expect 3.65-3.72M; AW=7 ~3.75M if area hurts).
  3. Time all three placement options against a same-session baseline
     (champion: 124.5 / 130.2 / 130.2). Ship only if cycles x median Fmax
     beats 318; record cycles, per-option Fmax and worst path in the notes.
Known risks: diffuse area/routing (+~2300 LUT4, r7s2: 2801 -> 5139) -
  fall back to AW=7 (4033) or AW=6; valid-flop 256:1 read mux (now ends at
  a flop, not at the compare); prev_fa_q gains 22 compare loads; table is
  never invalidated (immutable text, as r7s1/r7s2); the extra redirect
  bubble is a fixed ~3.9% cycle cost that buys nothing if the head mux
  would have been free - step 1 measures exactly that.

title: Next-instruction predictor without a head mux: registered IR fed by the bus at the NEXT pc, successor-word table in parallel at the IR D input
motivation:
Direction/target accuracy is exhausted (~55k redirects left, <= 1.3%), but
r7s2's next-instruction table (NIT: entry[P] = word of P's successor, exact
by tag + direction bit, no verify) is the largest IPC lever ever measured
here: 4,281,466 -> 3,536,081 cycles (+21% iter/cycle at AW=8; AW=7 3.606M,
AW=6 3.697M), formal 53/53 first try. It lost only because it was built on
the pre-r7s0 core and paid -10.6% Fmax (117.5 -> 105.0 MHz, 296.92).
Re-ported onto the 130.22 MHz champion (4,283,613 cycles) the same cycles
are worth ~368 at neutral Fmax and clear the 318.0 bar down to ~112.5 MHz.
But a straight re-port is fragile: r7s2 put a head mux
cur_instr = use_nb ? nb_instr_q : imem_data in front of ALL of decode, and
r7s0 left exactly those legs co-critical at 7.68 ns (imem_data -> op_a/op_b
D, 7-9 cells; pc_q -> PHT -> pc_q) - one more LUT + net there is ~0.9 ns
(-> ~115 MHz), and r7s2's own worst paths were flush_q (fanout 107) -> head
mux -> load-use compare -> stall and pc_q -> NIT -> 22-bit tag compare.
This hypothesis keeps the NIT's cycles but removes the head mux
topologically (r4s1 / r7s0 pattern: relocate to a register D input instead
of cutting depth in place), spending ~55k cycles (1.5%) to do so.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the instruction word a core register and move every word-source select
to its D input. if_stage state: pc_q (pc of the decode slot), ir_q (its
word), ir_v_q (word present). Decode, pre-decode, PHT, target adders and the
load-use compare all start at ir_q / pc_q flops (same depth as today's
imem_data flop, minus the `fa` mux in front of the adders).

The bus fetches the NEXT pc while the current word decodes:
  seq   = ir_v_q ? pc_q + 1 : pc_q                    (flops, syn_keep)
  na_nf = pred_taken ? tgt : seq                       (pred_taken gated by ir_v_q in its early legs)
  na    = flush_q ? flush_pc_q : na_nf ;  io_imemAddr = {na, 2'b00}
  adv   = flush_q | !ir_v_q | !stall                   (stall = load_use | dmem_stall | ex_busy)
  if (adv) pc_q <= na
  if (adv) ir_q   <= imem_ready ? imem_data : t_word   (select = bus-ready flop only)
  if (adv) ir_v_q <= imem_ready | nit_ok
No comb loop: na depends on ir_q, never on imem_data. imem_ready leaves the
stall chain completely (stall_if / kill_id lose their bus-pin term):
  kill_id = load_use | !ir_v_q | flush_q ;  hold_id = dmem_stall | ex_busy.
OOB safety (invariant 6; test/cosim/main.cpp flags ANY out-of-range
io_imemAddr, consumed or not): the bus now sees one address derived from a
wrong-path word. Behind a mispredicted branch that word is real code, but

title: EX loop routed-hop cut: per-byte replicated forward-select flops + one shared right shifter with the forward/reverse mux folded into its head (cycle-neutral Fmax)
motivation:
Arithmetic on logged numbers says no IPC micro-opt can clear the +4.6% bar
on the 357.06 champion (3,592,497 cycles): MUL busy is 94k cycles (2.6%,
and every preload variant cost >= its worth in Fmax, r6s0), store-side
dmem stalls ~1%, RAS ~0.7% (2 x 12.6k rets), the extra redirect bubble
~1.6% (r7s2 3,536,081 -> r8s1 3,592,497 = ~56k redirects), residual imem
~2.4%. LESSONS says the same: the next accepted change must gain Fmax.
The three micro_opt slots that WERE accepted (r1s0, r2s0, r7s0) were all
cycle-neutral critical-path cuts done as "cut the structurally longest
path, re-time all three options, repeat"; the two that failed (r4s0,
r8s0) shaved one LUT off every co-critical family at once or moved a mux
to a loop tail / RAM port.
The champion's scored worst path is the same on all three placement
options: ID/EX `fwd_a_ex` flop -> forward mux -> barrel shifter (two 4:1
stages + 2:1) -> result AND-OR -> EX/MEM.alu_result[23], 8-9 cells,
-2.925 ns slack, 128.27 MHz. Two things about it have never been
attacked:
  (1) it STARTS at a select flop, not a data flop: `fwd_a_ex` drives all
      32 alu_a muxes (more once Gowin folds the mux into the first
      shifter / logic / adder LUTs). r8s0 measured the sibling fanout-34
      `alu_sub` net at 3.4 ns in one build - a high-fanout select net is
      the slowest hop of the loop, and the four fwd_*_ex selects and
      shamt[1:0] are all of that kind;
  (2) the shifter is 5 general-routing hops (fwd LUT, l1, l2, final 2:1,
      AND-OR) although every one of its mux selects is a flop or one LUT
      behind a flop. Gowin CLS columns have dedicated MUX2_LUT5/6/7/8
      chains: a 16:1 mux is ONE routed stage (LUT4 -> MUX5 -> MUX6 ->
      MUX7 on dedicated wires), so the same function fits in 3 hops.
Neither edit changes a single cycle (CoreMark must stay at exactly
3,592,497), adds a RAM port, a new sink on decode / regfile read, or a
loop tail - the failure modes of r6s0/r6s1/r8s0.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Cut routed hops and select fanout on the EX ALU loop, in two separately
timed steps, each judged on a same-session three-option Gowin run
against the untouched champion (logged: 126.18 / 128.27 / 128.27 MHz).
RTL stays logic-equivalent, so formal 53/53 and the cycle count are
regression checks, not design risk.

Step 1 - replicated forward-select flops (id_stage.sv / core_pkg.sv /
ex_stage.sv, ~20 lines). ID/EX gets per-byte-lane copies of the selects
that head the loop:
    fwd_a_ex[3:0], fwd_b_ex[3:0]   (ALU operand muxes, lane k = bits 8k+7:8k)
    fwd_rs1_ex[1:0], fwd_rs2_ex[1:0] (compare / addr adder / store data;
                                      2 copies: one for the 16-bit halves)
all loaded with the same D (m_rs*_ex && a_is_reg / b_is_reg) and marked
`/* synthesis syn_preserve = 1 */` so Gowin does not merge them back
(the D logic is ~3 LUTs of flops and has slack: the D-stage families end
at op_a/op_b, not at these 1-bit flops). ex_stage uses copy k for lane k:
    alu_a[8k+:8] = in.fwd_a_ex[k] ? fwd_ex_mem[8k+:8] : in.op_a[8k+:8]
Each select net drops from fanout >= 32 to <= 8-16 and can be placed
next to its byte of the adder / shifter. If the attribute route is
simpler, try `syn_maxfan = 8` on the four existing flops first (one-line
variant) and keep whichever times better. `alu_sub` (fanout ~34: it
inverts every bx bit of the add/sub chain) gets the same per-byte
replication ONLY if the Step-1 timing report shows its first net on a
top-5 path; leave the adder itself alone.

Step 2 - shared right shifter with the forward mux folded into its head
(alu.sv / ex_stage.sv, ~40 lines; replaces l1/l2/shl + r1/r2/shr).
  * The shifter gets its OWN operand copy, taken from the two FLOPS, with
    the left-shift bit reversal merged into the same mux (selects are the
    flops fwd_a_ex and sel_shl, so this is one LUT4+MUX5 composite, no
    deeper than today's forward mux, and it takes 64 loads off alu_a):
      sh_in[i] = sel_shl ? (fwd_a ? F[31-i] : R[31-i])
                         : (fwd_a ? F[i]    : R[i])
    (F = EX/MEM.alu_result, R = ID/EX.op_a; pass both plus fwd_a into alu
    as extra ports or build sh_in in ex_stage).
  * One right shift by shamt[3:0] written as a single 16-way `case` per
    bit over {{16{fill}}, sh_in} so Gowin maps it onto the dedicated
    MUX5/6/7 chain (check the netlist: expect LUT4 -> MUX2_LUT5 ->
    MUX2_LUT6 -> MUX2_LUT7, not three LUT levels); fill = sh_arith &
    a[31] is only meaningful for sel_shr (0 for sel_shl by decode:
    sh_arith is set for SRA only).
  * shamt[4] (16-bit step) and the direction un-reverse are folded into
    the existing result AND-OR:
      out = sel_shr & (s4 ? {16{fill}},sh16[31:16] : sh16)
          | sel_shl & reverse(same)        // wiring + the existing AND
    i.e. per bit a 4:1 of sh16 taps with flop / one-LUT selects, feeding
    the same final OR as today.
  * shamt = alu_b[4:0] as now; if the report shows its nets on top, give
    shamt[3:0] the Step-1 treatment (two preserved copies of
    fwd_b_ex/op_b[3:0]/F[3:0] for the upper and lower 16 result bits).
  Hop count on the reported worst path: flop -> head mux -> 16:1 chain ->
  AND-OR -> flop (3 routed hops) instead of 5; area about -60 LUT4
  (one 16:1 x 32 = 256 LUT4 vs two shifters at ~5 x 64 = 320).
  Do NOT put syn_keep on any net inside the loop (r4s0: syn_keep on the
  ALU `rest` OR and on `br_cond` each cost 5-10%); the only attributes
  are syn_preserve on the replicated FLOPS.

Iterate, r7s0-style: after each step re-time all three options and read
the new worst path before touching anything else. Expected successors
and what NOT to do with them: `alu_sub -> add/sub carry -> alu_result`
(31 cells; r8s0's parallel a+b / a-b was a loss, leave it),
`IF/ID -> op_a/op_b D`, `pc_q -> PHT -> pc_q`, `EX/MEM.alu_result ->
compare -> flush_q` on option 0 (Step 1's fwd_rs*_ex copies are aimed at
it). If one of those is select-fanout-led (path begins at a 1-bit ID/EX
or IF/ID flop with a >1.5 ns first net), apply the same replicate-the-
select-flop cut and re-time; otherwise stop.

Decision rule: ship the variant with the best three-option median; keep

(2) fewer routed hops did not make a faster shifter on this part — one shared right shifter written as a 16-way `case` per bit over a flop-built, bit-reversed `sh_in`, with `shamt[4]` and the un-reverse folded into a one-hot 4-way AND-OR, passed cosim and an exhaustive SLL / SRL / SRA x 32-amount test and saved 65 LUT (5179 -> 5114) but cost 9% Fmax: its loop measured 10 cells instead of 8-9 (`alu_result_25 -> alu_result_10`, 14.051 ns on option 0) and on options 1/2 a 37-cell `alu_result_2 -> alu_result_0` path plus the dmem / IF-ID -> `op_a` families all sat at ~13.85 ns, i.e. the whole design slowed and the cause was not isolated (the implementer's reading, with the netlist's MUX2_LUT5/6/7 mapping never inspected and no first-net delays extracted, is that each dedicated mux counts as a cell while `shamt[0]` goes from ~128 to ~256 loads), so keep the two shared 4:1 stages unless a build first shows the 16:1 actually lands on the dedicated mux chain; the baseline's own top five (EX loop from `fwd_a_ex` / `fwd_b_ex`, `ifid_q.instr -> op_b`, `prev_fa_q` / `nb_tag_q -> nb_instr_q`, `fwd_rs2_ex -> flush_q`) sit within 5-8 ps of each other on every option, so a cut aimed at the one named worst path had no measurable headroom even had it worked, and a plan's "this D input has slack" should be checked by listing the baseline-report paths that END at that flop before any RTL is written (also not tried: `alu_sub` replication; formal was stopped before completion with no failures on Step 2 only, Step 1 and Step 1 + 2 were only linted and timed; the notes did not reach this record because the reverted RTL left an empty diff — figures are from the implementer's session log `.tmp/agent-logs/impl.hyp-20261125-001-r9s0.log`).
